key_insight: Training PV predictors to forecast multiple future time steps at once helps deep models learn longer-term temporal dependencies and improves accuracy beyond single-horizon prediction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable, low-overhead forecasting strategy for solar plants and grid operators to better manage PV intermittency and improve power-system stability.
method: Combine sequential sky imagery with historical PV generation data.
Use multi-horizon forecasting to predict several future PV output steps simultaneously.
Compare the approach across multiple deep learning architectures to test architecture-independent gains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comparative evaluation across diverse deep learning models, showing improved accuracy and robustness across the full forecast horizon with negligible extra computation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and availability of synchronized sky-image and PV-history data, so deployment will require careful sensor alignment and data coverage.
paper_title: Learning Long-Term Temporal Dependencies in Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Through Multi-Horizon Forecasting
